grade.reason: The agent's patch makes the same functional changes as the merged patch. It adds xsrf_cookie_name="_mitmproxy_xsrf" to the Application settings in app.py. It also changes the cookie lookup in web/src/js/utils.ts to "_mitmproxy_xsrf". The utils.ts change is identical to upstream. The extra changelog entry doesn't affect behavior.

result:
mitmweb now sets and reads its XSRF cookie as `_mitmproxy_xsrf`, so a stale HttpOnly `_xsrf` cookie in the browser no longer affects it. I didn't run any tests or the frontend build, as instructed.

- **Backend:** `mitmproxy/tools/web/app.py` now passes `xsrf_cookie_name="_mitmproxy_xsrf"` in the `Application` settings, next to `xsrf_cookies=True`.
- **Frontend:** `web/src/js/utils.ts` now reads `_mitmproxy_xsrf` instead of `_xsrf` when it fills the `X-XSRFToken` header in `fetchApi`.
- **Changelog:** I added an entry to `CHANGELOG.md`, without a PR reference.

I didn't add a test. The existing `test_app.py` turns XSRF checking off, so nothing there covers the cookie name.

The prebuilt bundle `mitmproxy/tools/web/static/index-Bt--WL1e.js` still reads `_xsrf`. It's a build artifact, so I left it alone, but it needs a frontend rebuild before it matches the new cookie name.
